trust_decision.summary: Which client session may get/result/list/cancel an experimental task is never decided: the default task handlers registered by enable_tasks() act on any task ID from any session against one shared TaskStore, and task IDs carry no creator identity.

landing_point.why: The summary names the experimental task handlers (get/result/list/cancel); _register_default_task_handlers is where all four live.

fix_sites.entry_point: JSON-RPC tasks/list (default handler); fix also stops forwarding the store cursor
tools/call with task augmentation -> ctx.experimental.run_task() (task ID minting now embeds session scope; explicit task_id deprecated)
fix_sites.module_kind: task-creation wrapper (producer of the identity the check reads)

fix_sites.entry_point: Server.run() per session -> TaskSupport.configure_session() (assigns per-session scope, none for stateless)
Server.run(..., stateless=...) used by streamable HTTP stateless mode
new module mcp.server.experimental.task_scope (ID format + scope predicates)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/mcp/server/experimental/request_context.py:213 (run_task mints the task ID via store.create_task -> src/mcp/shared/experimental/tasks/helpers.py:128) and src/mcp/server/experimental/task_support.py:99 / src/mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:670 (session setup, stateless flag)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about the tasks/* handlers; run_task, configure_session and Server.run's stateless path are 'task creation' and 'transport setup', so a solver can argue only the four handlers need a check, then has no creator identity to check against (or binds everything to the session and breaks stateless mode).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Stateless servers must keep serving a task to any later session that presents its ID (each request is a fresh session); tasks with explicit or store-created IDs stay reachable by ID from any session but are never listed; the creator must still poll/list/cancel its own tasks, including across more than one store page. A fix that binds every task to the creating session, or rejects unknown-scope IDs, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: explicitly chosen task_id passed to run_task (unscoped, accessible by ID, never listed)
task created on a stateless session (requestor scope None)
scoped-looking but malformed IDs: uppercase hex, non-uuid suffix, trailing newline (\Z anchor)
tasks/list spanning multiple store pages, with the store cursor (another task's ID) withheld from the requestor

O7_producer.where: task ID generation: src/mcp/shared/experimental/tasks/helpers.py:107 via src/mcp/shared/experimental/tasks/in_memory_task_store.py:80 called from src/mcp/server/experimental/request_context.py:213; tasks/list cursor producer src/mcp/shared/experimental/tasks/in_memory_task_store.py:182 (cursor is a raw task ID)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Shared TaskResultHandler is registered as response router on every session and resolves pending task elicitation/sampling requests by request ID with no session check, so a response from another session can complete a task's queued input.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is response routing, not a tasks/* request; the request ID embeds id(params) so it looks unguessable.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 2 files from landing point, packages mcp.server.experimental and mcp.server

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Public lower-level TaskResultHandler.handle() serves any task's queued messages and result to the calling session; the fix only adds a docstring saying custom callers must decide access.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Lower-level API used by custom handlers; the default handler is guarded before calling it.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Public cancel_task(store, task_id) helper, shown in its own docstring as the body of a custom tasks/cancel handler, has no requestor scoping.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Shared store helper with no session context; custom handlers are the server author's responsibility.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A task-progress or task-status notification route that looks a task up by client-supplied ID without the scope check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ServerTaskContext already does store lookups and queueing keyed only by task_id; a maintainer adding a status/progress feature would copy that pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A store-level filter or delete route (e.g. tasks/delete or a list filter by status) taking a raw task ID or cursor.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The store exposes delete_task and cursor-by-task-ID pagination; a new default handler wrapping them would naturally omit scoping.

O9_family: missing authorization / cross-tenant object access (IDOR, CWE-862)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/experimental/tasks/ (server/test_server.py, server/test_task_result_handler.py, test_request_context.py); in-memory streams, no network

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Record the creating session (or session id) in a server-side map and reject every tasks/* request from any other session, which breaks stateless mode and unscoped-ID access, and keeps forwarding the store cursor (another session's task ID) in tasks/list.

out_of_scope_notes: Client-side default task handlers (src/mcp/client/experimental/task_handlers.py) serve a single peer server; not a multi-tenant surface.
Explicit task_id tasks stay globally reachable by ID by design (deprecated, documented in fix.diff:22-29).
